newsitem.title: INDIA: Chidambaram return helps Bombay shares end higher.
newsitem.headline: Chidambaram return helps Bombay shares end higher.

text.p: Bombay shares ended higher on Wednesday but well off their peak as profit-booking sliced into a sharp early rally made on news former finance minister P. Chidambaram was returning to the government.
"I think people took advantage of the early enthusiasm and decided to book profits in a strong market," said Maulik Sharedalal, member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange.
A decision by G.K. Moopanar, leader of Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC), to take his party back into the government spread cheer across the market, dealers said.
"It's a good move and should boost investor confidence," said Aditya Rattan, chief representative at Daiwa Securities.
TMC had earlier opted to stay out of the new government after Moopanar was passed over as the choice for prime minister.
Government officials have said Chidambaram was due to return to the cabinet as finance minister.
Technical problems delayed the start of trading at the BSE on Wednesday.
All the exchanges will be closed on Thursday for a national holiday.
Share prices are seen consolidating around current levels, with investment buying expected to pick up in good quality stocks, traders said.
"It'll be a slow and steady rise to the 4,000 mark," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs.
"They are sticking to their universe of stocks, picking up blue chips," Jhaveri said commenting on foreign fund action.
Fund managers said fundamental factors like falling interest rates, triggered by an easier central bank monetary policy announced this month would encourage investment buying.
"Liquidity is improving," said Gul Teckchandani, chief investment officer at Sun Foreign & Coloniarl Asset Management. "I think investment decisions will take place at these levels,"
"From a 12-18 month time frame, price valuations are very attractive."
"We expect interest rates to decline, especially at the long end, triggering a rally in stocks," Morgan Stanley analyst Pravin Shah said in a country report.
Most banks have cut their prime lending rates to 14.0-16 percent from 14.5-17.5 percent.
Market focus will now shift to company results for 1996/97 which are due in the next two months, analysts said.
"Corporate results are now the key factor for markets," said M. R. Madhavan, market strategist at ICICI Securites & Finance Company Ltd. (I-Sec).
"Our earnings expectation for the BSE Sensex stocks is a growth of about three percent as compared to a 30 pct rise in the previous year."
However, consensus market estimates for the Sensex stocks were slightly higher at about 6-7 percent, Madhavan said.
"There's nothing great happening. The market should move in a band of 200 points, either side," he said.
Shares of Housing Development and Finance Corporation (HDFC) fell 120.0 rupees from highs to close at 3,160.0 on profit-taking after the firm announced results, traders said.
HDFC closed down 12.25 rupees from Tuesday.
The company said its net profit for the year ending March 31 1997 rose 27 percent to 2.48 billion rupees from 1.96 billion in the year-ago period.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
